outcome: No case of the stated conjecture (invertibility of the n-by-n matrix/linear independence of the n polynomials for a configuration of n points in R^3, for n beyond the already-settled n=4) has been proved since 26 January 2024. Two post-window papers touch adjacent territory but both change the problem rather than settling any of it: Malkoun (arXiv 2508.13472, Aug 2025) generalizes the Atiyah problem and Atiyah-Sutcliffe conjectures 1 and 2 to a 'G-amplitude function' framework over finite graphs, recovering the classical conjectures only as the special case G = K_n, without proving that special case for any new n; and Guerra-Salvatore (arXiv 2410.24124, Oct 2024, published in Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A, Aug 2026) show that the Atiyah-Sutcliffe conjecture would imply an E3-algebra structure on flag manifolds, a structural/implicational result rather than a proof of any case.
summary: The Atiyah conjecture on configurations (that the n-by-n matrix / n associated polynomials for n distinct points in R^3 are always linearly independent, equivalently the Atiyah determinant is never zero) remains open for general n. It was proved for n<=4 by Eastwood-Norbury (2001) and reproved by an alternate method by Malkoun (2022/2023), both before the frozen revision date and already reflected in the pre-2024 literature. Since 26 January 2024, two arXiv items surfaced in searches, and I opened both directly (not just the triage snippets). The first, Malkoun's August 2025 preprint (2508.13472), builds a generalized 'G-amplitude function' framework using finite graphs and tensors; it explicitly recovers the Atiyah-Sutcliffe conjectures 1 and 2 only when the graph G is taken to be the complete graph K_n, i.e. the classical conjecture is a special case of the new, broader conjectural framework the paper proposes — it does not prove that special case for any n beyond what was already known, so per the scope rule (§3.1) this is a related/generalizing problem, not a case of the stated conjecture. The second, Guerra-Salvatore's 'The Atiyah-Sutcliffe conjecture and En-algebras' (arXiv 2410.24124, submitted 31 Oct 2024, v2 5 Nov 2024, published in Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A on 28 Aug 2026), proves that the conjecture (if true) would imply an E3-algebra structure on the disjoint union of flag manifolds, and does homological calculations around this; it is an implication/structural connection to algebraic topology, not a proof of any new case, and does not move the truth value of the conjecture in either direction. I also checked for any claimed disproof or counterexample: a superficially similar-sounding paper, 'Atiyah's Minkowski Space Conjecture Fails for Every n>=3' (arXiv 2608.16693, Aug 2026), does refute a conjecture by Atiyah, but on close reading this is a distinct 'Minkowski space' variant concerning worldlines and celestial directions in Minkowski space, not the Euclidean R^3 configuration conjecture stated in this bullet — it changes the ambient space and objects (worldlines vs. points), so under §3.1 it is a related problem with a different namesake, not a case of this one. I found no mention of any AI system, LLM, or automated theorem-proving tool in any of the sources checked (the two 2024/2025 preprints, Malkoun's blog, or general searches for AI-assisted work on this problem); all work is traditional algebraic/geometric mathematics, in the latter case combined with algebraic topology. I also checked the problem's current Wikipedia article, which remains a stub with no discussion of recent results. On balance the correct classification is open, no_change_found true.
competing_reading: One could argue the Malkoun 2025 generalization deserves 'progress' rather than 'open' on the theory that a conjectural framework which reduces to the original conjecture as a special case is itself a step toward the original. But no instance of the original n-point conjecture beyond n=4 is proved by this framework, so nothing about what a careful reader would write in this bullet's entry (the invertibility claim for n points in R^3) has changed; it remains a related problem under the stated rule, and I classify it as no_change_found rather than progress.
what_would_settle_it: A proof (or disproof/counterexample) of the invertibility claim for some n=5 or a proof of the general case, published or preprinted after 26 January 2024, framed in terms of the original R^3 point-configuration determinant rather than a generalized or differently-set variant.
